limits_source: FAO EcoCrop sheet 1574: absolute and optimal limits for temperature, soil pH and texture.
cycle_source: Pinoy Rice Knowledge Bank (PhilRice), NSIC Rc222 (Tubigan 18): matures in 106 days direct seeded, 114 days transplanted. https://www.pinoyrice.com/rice-varieties/ . Chosen because Rc222 and Rc216 are reported as the most planted inbreds in Nueva Ecija (Glover et al. 2020, Technology in Society 60:101227); Rc216 is 104/112 days, so the choice between them moves little. Days are counted FROM SEEDING: for transplanted rice this includes the seedbed, so 114 overstates time in the field. Rc222 is on the site's irrigated list; the rainfed option NSIC Rc192 (Sahod Ulan 1) also matures in 106 days after seeding, so the short figure holds for a rainfed variety too. Replaces EcoCrop sheet 1574's 80-180 days.
kc_source: FAO-56 T12 rice Kc 1.05/1.20/0.90-0.60; used 0.90 (upper end; FAO-56 gives no rule for picking within the range). T11 30/30/60/30 = 150 d, Dec/May, Tropics. Paddy seepage follows the field's soil texture: 4 mm/d heavy clay, 8 mm/d sandy, 6 mm/d on average (used for medium soils; that reading is ours), from FAO Irrigation Water Management Training Manual 3 ch.4 (NOT FAO-56; FAO-56 does not model paddy water balance). The 4.0 in percolation_mm_day only marks rice as a paddy crop; the model takes the figure for the soil. Manual 3's 200 mm saturation and 100 mm water layer are NOT included, so rice demand is understated. Kc NOT climate-adjusted (Eq. 62/65).
